The seventh beta of CoSky 8.0, still for developers to try. It carries the fixes an audit of beta.6 found, and moves to Spring Boot 4.2.0 and Spring Cloud 2026.0.0. The stable release is still 6.x, on the [`v6`](https://github.com/Ahoo-Wang/CoSky/tree/v6) branch.

There is no compatibility promise before `8.0.0-rc.1`, which freezes what [`CONTRIBUTING.md`](https://github.com/Ahoo-Wang/CoSky/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#releases-and-versioning) lists. This beta asks applications on the starter to move to Spring Boot 4.2 and Spring Cloud 2026.0, and its notes say how. The gRPC and REST APIs, the wire format, the properties and the data in Redis are unchanged.

## Try it

[Getting Started](https://cosky.ahoo.me/guide/getting-started) takes a few minutes: a server in development mode, a Spring Boot application that reads a Config and registers, and another that finds it.

```bash
docker run -p 8080:8080 -p 9090:9090 ahoowang/cosky:8.0.0-beta.7 --dev
```

What helps most is still what we could only try on one machine: Redis Sentinel or Cluster of your own with a failover, an OIDC provider other than Keycloak, moving a 6.x installation with `cosky-migrate`, and a real network. [Tell us](https://github.com/Ahoo-Wang/CoSky/issues/new/choose) what breaks or surprises you.

## Fixed

- **A Namespace creation that came late could bring a deleted namespace back.**
  - A creation writes the Namespace object first, then makes the namespace. One that stopped in between could go on after the reconciler had finished it and the namespace had been deleted. It then made the namespace again, with no object: invisible in the list and to the reconciler, and open to writes.
  - Now, once it has made the namespace, a creation reads the object again as of the store's latest write. If the object is gone, or marked by the deletion of an earlier namespace, the creation came late, and it drops what it made. The request and the reconciler both go this way, and so does an epoch replaced meanwhile. (#1262, #1268)
- **After a refresh that failed, a change to some other property could remove Configs still imported.** A refresh that failed half way, say on a Config that does not parse, keeps the Environment as it was. But the next `EnvironmentChangeEvent` of anything else, such as a property set through the `env` endpoint, took what that refresh had loaded so far for all the imports load. The Configs it had not got to left the Environment, and their watches ended. Now only a run of the imports that went through counts. (#1263)
- **A new client with no snapshot could stay on a replica that cannot read its store.** Its first watch waited for that replica to load the namespace, which never happened, while the replica's progress messages kept the client there. The healthy endpoint after it was never tried. Now a first watch still waits out a slow load, but a load that fails ends the stream with `UNAVAILABLE`, and the client goes to the next endpoint. A watch with a position does so at once too. (#1264)
- **A rollback with a malformed `toRevision` was a 500, and `[1]` rolled back.** Now only a number or a string is taken. `null`, an object, an array, or a value out of range is a 400 that changes nothing. (#1265)

## Changed

- **Spring Boot 4.2.0 and Spring Cloud 2026.0.0.** Spring Cloud 2026.0 declares Spring Boot 4.2, so its compatibility verifier no longer has to be turned off. Spring gRPC is still 1.1.2, and with it gRPC 1.84 and protobuf 4.36. (#1267)

## Upgrading from beta.6

- **Applications on the starter move to Spring Boot 4.2.0 and Spring Cloud 2026.0.0,** as [Requirements](https://cosky.ahoo.me/guide/requirements) says:

  ```kotlin
  implementation(platform("org.springframework.boot:spring-boot-dependencies:4.2.0"))
  implementation(platform("org.springframework.cloud:spring-cloud-dependencies:2026.0.0"))
  ```

  Then remove `spring.cloud.compatibility-verifier.enabled: false`, which Spring Cloud 2025.1 needed.
- **WebClient follows the proxy system properties on Spring Boot 4.2.** The JDK on macOS sets them from the system's proxy, whose exceptions may come as ranges that Reactor Netty does not read. A load-balanced call to an instance's address may then go through that proxy. Where it should not, set `-Dhttp.nonProxyHosts` to hosts the client can read, such as `10.*|192.168.*|*.internal`.
- Nothing else changes: the gRPC API, the protos, REST, the data in Redis and the properties. `cosky-migrate` and the Dashboard come with this release.

## Known limits

- **Tried on one laptop, not in a data center:** the Cluster and Sentinel failovers, the scale and the emulated network on the [Performance](https://cosky.ahoo.me/guide/performance) page. OIDC was tried with Keycloak 26 only.
- **On Sentinel,** while a master that hangs still holds the connection hints come on, each replica reads every namespace every second instead. A write then takes up to a second to reach watchers.
- **At rest, each replica reads each namespace once a second,** in case a hint was lost. On one Redis, 5,000 namespaces and three replicas took 30% of its CPU. A Cluster, or a longer `cosky.store.redis.tail-poll-interval`, lowers it.
- **Writes over a lossy network:** where 1% of packets are lost, a write's p99 is above 200 ms, as TCP waits to resend a lost packet.
- **A replica cut off from Redis on its own** goes on serving what it last knew, and stays ready. [Deployment](https://cosky.ahoo.me/guide/deployment) shows how to notice.
- **A late Namespace creation that takes a write before it is undone** stays, without an object, and the server logs an error. That takes a write in the round trip between making the namespace and dropping it.
- **Removing every CoSky import at once** leaves their properties in place. A refresh that loaded no CoSky Config at all is not taken as one that ran the imports, so that nothing is dropped by mistake.
- **The server does not stop an account from granting itself roles** it may write; see the security guide.
